title: Microsoft Purview DLP: act on classification failures in Exchange Online
summary: Hold: the briefing overstates the reach of a blocking scan-failure rule by saying it applies to every message with that failure type. Microsoft documents policy scoping and enforcement-mode qualifications; the default, enabling control, licensing background and roadmap details are otherwise supported.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Exchange Online DLP policies can detect and act on classification failures when the classification service cannot fully scan an attachment.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview data loss prevention (DLP) policies for Exchange Online can detect and act on classification failures—cases where the classification service can't fully scan a document.

claims.claim: The feature's Learn page is titled Configure default protection for classification failures in Data loss prevention for Exchange (preview) and documents preview behaviour.
claims.quote: Configure default protection for classification failures in Data loss prevention for Exchange (preview)

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Classification failure detection is admin-opt-in, so its expanded detection does not start until an administrator enables it.
claims.quote: By default, these conditions detect only text extraction failures. After you enable classification failure detection, they also detect classification failures such as timeouts, throttling, and other errors.

claims.claim: The improved attachment conditions are Document couldn't be scanned and Document didn't complete scanning.
claims.quote:
| Document couldn't be scanned | Text extraction failures
| Document didn't complete scanning | Partial text extraction

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: With detection off, these conditions detect text extraction failures rather than classification failures.
claims.quote: By default, these conditions detect only text extraction failures.

claims.claim: Text extraction failure examples include a file that cannot be opened, an unsupported format and a password-protected file.
claims.quote: Text extraction failures (for example, the file couldn't be opened, the format is unsupported, or the file is password protected).

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Enabling detection adds classification failures caused by timeouts, throttling and other errors to the scan conditions.
claims.quote: After you enable classification failure detection, they also detect classification failures such as timeouts, throttling, and other errors.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: DocumentScanFailures lets rules take different actions for Timeout, Throttled and Other classification failure types.
claims.quote: To take different actions for specific classification failure types—Timeout, Throttled, or Other—use the DocumentScanFailures condition.

claims.claim: DocumentScanFailures must be combined with either of the two scan conditions using AND.
claims.quote: Combine it with either Document couldn't be scanned or Document didn't complete scanning using AND

claims.claim: DocumentScanFailures cannot be used on its own.
claims.quote: DocumentScanFailures can't be used on its own.

claims.where: controls[0].note; What's changing; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: The classification failure detection setting applies only to Exchange Online.
claims.quote: This setting applies to Exchange Online only.

claims.claim: The setting does not affect SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams or Endpoint DLP policies.
claims.quote: It doesn't affect SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams, or Endpoint DLP policies.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Existing rules using the scan conditions may have more DLP rule matches after detection is enabled.
claims.quote: If your tenant already has rules that use these conditions, you might see an increase in DLP rule matches after you enable detection.

claims.claim: Scan-failure rules detect failures only from classifiers DLP has already evaluated.
claims.quote: Scan-failure rules detect failures only from classifiers that DLP has already evaluated.

claims.claim: A classifier failure in a content-detection rule placed after a scan-failure rule can be missed by that scan-failure rule.
claims.quote: If a content-detection rule is placed after a scan-failure rule and its classifier fails, the failure won't be detected.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout, After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Microsoft advises putting content-detection rules at higher priority than scan-failure rules.
claims.quote: To avoid missed detections, order your rules so that content-detection rules (sensitive information types, exact data matches, and trainable classifiers) have higher priority than scan-failure rules (Timeout, Throttled, Other)

claims.claim: The feature page describes no new identity or permission model.
claims.quote: Searched: "classification failure detection" "per-user" "per-policy" "permissions"; read the complete classification-failure protection page, which describes portal and Security & Compliance PowerShell configuration but no new identity model.

claims.claim: Classification failure detection is an organisation-level setting rather than a rule-level switch.
claims.quote: from the Microsoft Purview portal, go to Settings on the left navigation menu > Data loss prevention > Scan failure settings for Exchange. In Scan failure settings for Exchange turn on the toggle.

claims.claim: The feature page names no per-user or per-policy scope for the detection setting.
claims.quote: Searched: "classification failure detection" "per-user" "per-policy" "permissions"; read the complete classification-failure protection page and the Set-PolicyConfig syntax. Neither describes per-user or per-policy scoping for this setting.

claims.claim: Protection actions are configured in DLP rules rather than determined solely by enabling detection.
claims.quote: Actions define what happens as a consequence of a condition being met.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The Learn example uses Block for content rules and Audit for Timeout, Throttled and Other scan-failure rules.
claims.quote:
| 1 | Detect credit cards | Content contains Credit Card Number | Block |
| 4 | Full scan timeout | DocumentIsUnsupported AND DocumentScanFailures = Timeout | Audit |

claims.claim: A block action on a scan-failure condition would apply to every message whose attachment hits that failure type.
claims.quote: Whether an action takes effect or not depends on how you configure the mode of the policy.
claims.fix: Remove the sentence 'A block action on a scan-failure condition would apply to every message whose attachment hits that failure type.' The unconditional 'every message' disregards policy scope, policy mode and the classifier-ordering limitation already described on the page.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Change & support; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Microsoft advises allowing up to one hour for the detection setting to synchronise before validating policy behaviour.
claims.quote: Allow up to one hour for the setting change to synchronize across the service before validating policy behavior.

claims.claim: The enabling control is reached in Microsoft Purview portal through Settings > Data loss prevention > Scan failure settings for Exchange.
claims.quote: go to Settings on the left navigation menu > Data loss prevention > Scan failure settings for Exchange. In Scan failure settings for Exchange turn on the toggle.
claims.fix: Extend controls[0].ui.path and the matching rendered table path to 'Settings > Data loss prevention > Scan failure settings for Exchange > toggle'. The source gives an unlabelled toggle on that page; the current route correctly reaches the page but stops before the control.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls table; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: Set-PolicyConfig -DlpErrorHandlingConfig $json configures detection through Security & Compliance PowerShell as documented on the feature page.
claims.quote:
Connect to Security & Compliance PowerShell and run the following commands.
Connect-IPPSSession
$json = '{"Classification":{"State":1}}'  # To disable, set State to 0
Set-PolicyConfig -DlpErrorHandlingConfig $json

claims.claim: The JSON string {"Classification":{"State":1}} enables classification failure detection.
claims.quote:
$json = '{"Classification":{"State":1}}'  # To disable, set State to 0
Set-PolicyConfig -DlpErrorHandlingConfig $json

claims.claim: Setting State to 0 with the same command disables detection.
claims.quote: $json = '{"Classification":{"State":1}}'  # To disable, set State to 0
